prerequisites: Competencies taught in the modules Object-Oriented Programming and Graphics Programming are recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Students can describe and apply methods for creating high-visual-quality computer-generated images; this includes topics such as modeling a dynamic virtual scene, free-form curves and surfaces, global illumination techniques, or methods for visualizing volume data.

Students can explain the architecture of current graphics cards and understand the graphics card as an enormously powerful stream processor with many parallel processing units that can also be used for complex computations outside of computer graphics.
Students can apply parallel programming on the graphics card.
Students are able to apply scientific working methods in independently identifying, formulating, and solving problems.
Students are able to speak freely about scientific content, both in front of an audience and in a discussion.

assessment_methods.method: Oral presentation of solutions to at least two exercise assignments

assessment_rules: To acquire credit points, students must achieve at least 50 percent of the points from the weekly exercise assignments and orally present the solution to at least two of these assignments. The examination is either an oral examination or a written examination. Grading is based on a scale of 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the M.Sc. Computer Science degree program.
